∆ιαφέρει δὲ τοῦ μυελοῦ ὁ ἐγκέφαλος καὶ ἀνελυπεὶς καὶ ἀναίματος, ὁ δὲ μυελὸς,
ῥυπαρὸς καὶ αἱματώδης. Τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ τεσσάρων στοιχείων συνίσταται,
ἐπειδὴ ἔχει ἐν ἑαυτῷ αἷμα, φλέγμα, χολὴν ξανθὴν, καὶ χολὴν μέλαιναν. Ἕκαστον δὲ
τούτων τὸν ἴδιον τόπον δημιουργεῖ· τὸ αἷμα εἰς τὸ δεξιὸν μέρος ἐπάνω τοῦ ἥπατος· ἡ
χολὴ ἡ ξανθὴ εἰς τὸ ἀριστερὸν μέρος ἐπάνω τῆς σπλήνης· ἡ δὲ χολὴ ἡ μελαίνη εἰς
τὰς ψόας ἐπάνω τῶν νεφρῶν· τὸ δὲ φλέγμα εἰς τὸ στῆθος ἐπάνω τοῦ 95.245
πνεύματος. Καὶ τὸ μὲν αἷμα ἐστὶ θερμὸν καὶ ὑγρὸν καὶ γλυκύ· χολὴ ἡ ξανθὴ ἐστὶ
θερμή ....

thought_title: Brain versus marrow, and the four humors and their seats
orientation: John of Damascus is closing his account of human nature by contrasting the brain with marrow and then restating the four elements and where each humor builds its own place in the body.
pass_a_gloss: And the brain differs from the marrow, both painless and bloodless, but the marrow [is] dirty and bloody. The body of the human being is composed of four elements, since it has in itself blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile. And each of these builds its own place: the blood into the right part above the liver; the yellow bile into the left part above the spleen; and the black bile into the loins above the kidneys; and the phlegm into the chest above the breath. And the blood is warm and moist and sweet; the yellow bile is warm ...

choices.why: The adjective means free from pain or grief; rendering it as 'without pain' keeps the privative force of the alpha prefix visible.
The privative alpha plus haima means lacking blood; 'without blood' preserves the parallel structure with 'without pain'.
The word means filthy or unclean; 'dirty' is the plainest literal equivalent and matches the contrast with the brain's purity.
The suffix -odes means full of or characterized by; 'bloody' captures the sense of being full of blood, contrasting with the brain's lack of blood.
The verb means to create or fashion; 'builds' conveys the active making of a place for each humor without importing theological overtones of 'create'.
Pneuma here is the vital breath or spirit in the chest; 'breath' is the literal sense and avoids the interpretive 'spirit'.

pass_b_english: The brain differs from marrow in being without sorrow and bloodless, while marrow is dirty and full of blood. The human body is composed of four elements, since it contains blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile. Each of these builds its own place: blood on the right side above the liver, yellow bile on the left side above the spleen, black bile in the loins above the kidneys, and phlegm in the chest above the breath. Blood is warm, moist, and sweet; yellow bile is warm...

fixed: The Greek ἀνελυπεὶς means 'painless' or 'free from pain,' not 'without sorrow'; the English now reads 'painless and bloodless.'
The Greek uses εἰς with the accusative for the humor seats, meaning 'into' or 'in,' not 'on'; the English now reads 'in the right part above the liver,' etc.
The Greek text breaks off after 'θερμή' (warm); the English now marks the break with '[text breaks off]'.

The glossary entries for humor seats reflect different sections of the source; the current passage gives the seats as above the liver, above the spleen, in the loins above the kidneys, and in the chest above the breath, which the English now follows exactly.

problems.quote: The temple, then, is the ruler of the body
problems.why: Three different words for same ruling bodily part; reader may think 'temple' is distinct from head/brain.
problems.fix: Use 'head' or 'brain' consistently; gloss 'temple' if translating Greek hegemonikon.

problems.quote: It is composed of four elements: namely, blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile
